hints: Separate the variables by dividing by $x/5+1$, leaving the $\theta$ expression on the other side.
Integrate the $x$-side logarithmically and retain the factor arising from $x/5+1$.
Apply $x=5$ when $\theta=0$ to determine the constant, then exponentiate and isolate $x$.
walkthrough:
Separate variables by multiplying by $\dfrac{5}{x + 5}$ and by $\mathrm{d}\theta$:
$$\dfrac{5}{x + 5}\,\mathrm{d}x = \sin^2(2\theta)\,\mathrm{d}\theta$$

Use the double-angle identity $\sin^2 A = \dfrac{1 - \cos(2A)}{2}$ with $A = 2\theta$:
$$\sin^2(2\theta) = \dfrac{1 - \cos(4\theta)}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(4\theta)$$
$$\dfrac{5}{x + 5}\,\mathrm{d}x = \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(4\theta)\right)\,\mathrm{d}\theta$$

Substitute the initial condition $x = 5$ when $\theta = 0$ to find the constant $c$:
$$5\ln(5 + 5) = \dfrac{1}{2}(0) - \dfrac{1}{8}\sin(0) + c$$
$$5\ln(10) = 0 - 0 + c \implies c = 5\ln 10$$

Substitute $c = 5\ln 10$ and rearrange the logarithmic terms:
$$5\ln(x + 5) = \dfrac{1}{2}\theta - \dfrac{1}{8}\sin(4\theta) + 5\ln 10$$
$$5\ln(x + 5) - 5\ln 10 = \dfrac{1}{2}\theta - \dfrac{1}{8}\sin(4\theta)$$
$$5\ln\left(\dfrac{x + 5}{10}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\theta - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin(4\theta)\right)$$

Divide by 5 to isolate the logarithm:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{x + 5}{10}\right) = \dfrac{1}{10}\left(\theta - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin(4\theta)\right)$$

Exponentiate both sides to express $x$ in terms of $\theta$:
$$\dfrac{x + 5}{10} = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{10}\left(\theta - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin(4\theta)\right)\right]$$
$$x + 5 = 10\exp\left[\dfrac{1}{10}\left(\theta - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin(4\theta)\right)\right]$$
$$x = 10\exp\left[\dfrac{1}{10}\left(\theta - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin(4\theta)\right)\right] - 5$$
